subject: future
topic: How many jobs can today's AI already touch?
angle: While AI exposure varies significantly across different job categories, it is more likely to create a combination of human and LLM-driven work rather than simple substitution.
title: The Hybrid Work Reality

hooks.text: Which jobs will AI actually touch?
You expect total replacement. The evidence shows a hybrid shift.
You are learning to work with a machine.
A cursor blinks on a blank page.

reveal.headline: AI exposure varies from 9.4 to 81.7 percent.
reveal.body: The impact of AI depends on your specific job category. Some roles show nearly total exposure, while others show very little. This evidence is mixed and based on preliminary studies.

explain.headline: Substitution is not the only path.
explain.body: Economic factors may create a combination of human and LLM-driven work rather than simple replacement. Human-in-the-loop verification is linked to higher performance in some cases.

matters.headline: Your role may evolve into a hybrid.
matters.body: That may be why your work feels different. You might not be replaced by a machine. Instead, your tasks may become a collaboration between your judgment and an LLM.

example.headline: A screen reflects a new workflow.
example.body: You sit at your desk. You type a prompt. You review the output and correct the errors before you hit send. You are the filter for the machine.

question.headline: Which part of your work remains uniquely yours?

stat.label: the maximum category-level coverage of AI exposure across 22 major groups

claims.text: Some occupations register zero measured exposure purely for lack of chat traffic, which could be due to a slower adoption-lag.
claims.quote: Anthropic’s own report naming occupations that register zero measured exposure purely for lack of chat traffic – though it cannot, on cross-sectional evidence alone, be distinguished from a slower adoption-lag explanation.

claims.text: Large language models can lead to more sustainable alternatives to current practices, but economic factors may cause a new combination of human and LLM-driven work rather than simple substitution.
claims.quote: economic factors may cause widespread adoption to lead to a new combination of human and LLM-driven work, rather than a simple substitution.

claims.text: Category-level coverage of AI exposure varies from 9.4 to 81.7 percent across 22 SOC major groups.
claims.quote: Category-level coverage varies substantially (9. 4 to 81. 7 percent across 22 SOC major groups), supporting neither the claim that any category is immune to AI nor that any nears full automation.

claims.text: ChatGPT shows promise in streamlining some jobs, especially those requiring memorization, but it also presents challenges like ethical implications and AI security.
claims.quote: Findings revealed ChatGPT’s promise in streamlining some jobs, especially those requiring memorization. Moreover, we highlighted ChatGPT’s challenges and limitations, such as ethical implications, LLM limitations, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) security.

claims.text: A GenAI-assisted package with human-in-the-loop verification was associated with higher case-analysis performance and greater behavioral engagement in one nonrandomized cohort.
claims.quote: A multicomponent GenAI-assisted, 4-act progressive-disclosure CBL package implemented with rigorous human-in-the-loop verification was associated with higher case-analysis performance, modestly higher delayed examination performance, and greater behavioral engagement in one nonrandomized cohort.

verdict: The evidence shows that AI impacts vary widely by occupation and may lead to complex human-AI collaborations rather than total automation.
caveat: Many findings are based on preliminary studies, nonrandomized cohorts, or lack peer review.
caption:
AI exposure varies significantly across different job categories.

Research shows that while AI can streamline tasks, it often leads to a combination of human and LLM-driven work. These findings are based on preliminary studies and nonrandomized cohorts.
